print_rules: Native 1920x1080 at 24 fps; sub-pixel motion everywhere; no pixel grid, no nearest-neighbour, no dithering.

One halftone screen for the film: round dots, 45 degrees, 8 px period (three/engine/print.js uPeriod 8). Dots carry shading, gradients, skies and AM glows only (glow: 12-20 px period, coverage 80% at the source to 5% at ~300 px). Lit planes are flat ink, so flights never turn into screen-door noise.

2D layers carry their dots with them (dots move with parallax, as in the reference). In three.js shots drive uJitter from the camera's screen-space pan so big pans drag the dot field with the image; on fast flights the shading dots fall back to flat ink bands.
12-32 inks per shot from the shot's colour world; darkest #1A1416, lightest #F6F2E7 or #EDE3CF; never pure black or pure white.
Paper: one fixed scan (fibres + mottling), multiply 6%, never regenerated per frame; it rides the gate jitter.

Gate jitter applied last to the whole frame including type: new random offset every 2-3 frames (occasionally 5), 0.6-1.6 px (median 0.9), held between jumps; +-1% stepped luminance flicker on each jump.
Vignette flat to 0.55 of the half-diagonal, then linear to x0.80 at the corners. Grain: luma only, 1-3 px, +-3%.
No scanlines, no frame curvature, no chromatic aberration, no global bloom. Glows are designed per element. Misregistration only where a shot asks for it.

LED layer: real dot-matrix, round LEDs with a 2 px soft core and a dark ring, unlit dots visible at 12%; on-screen pitch 10-18 px; Latin 5x7, Japanese 16x16 dot font (Shinonome/JF-Dot 16 style); train board #F08A3C, vending/clock/TV #7FC8B8, pool scoreboard #F5C842. Scrolling is dot-locked (whole dots per frame): the only grid-locked element in the film.
Every shot has at least three independent motion sources (camera, character, secondary: wires, fan, curtain, water, crowd, particles). No still image is ever just pushed in on.
Master encode at 20 Mbps or more so the 8 px dots and dark flats survive (the reference's 4 Mbps turned dark flats into macroblocks).

typography_rules.japanese: Shippori Mincho B1 ExtraBold, vertical. Main lyric glyph 100 px (column ~120 px with outline) at x~1720, first glyph y~160; lead glyphs 40 px; emphasis 180-230 px. Style A: cream #EDE3CF fill, 3 px warm-black #1A1416 line, offset shadow (+7,+7) in the world's accent ink (night/dusk/festival vermilion #D9402B, noon cobalt #2D6BE0, dream heat orange #F08A3C). Style B on busy plates: warm-black glyph with an 8 px cream outline.
typography_rules.entrance: 見当合わせ registration snap: each glyph arrives as two misregistered plates (fill + shadow, 24 px apart) that lock together in 2 frames, on its sung mora (vocal-stem onset detection; fallback: even spacing over 85% of the line). Exit: the glyph breaks into its halftone dots, which shrink away over 6 frames.
typography_rules.chinese: Noto Serif SC SemiBold 30-34 px, cream at 85%, a thin vertical column left of the Japanese column (horizontal under the board for LED lines); the whole line fades in over 6 frames at the vocal onset and exits with the Japanese.
typography_rules.english: English lines run on LED dot-matrix boards (5x7 caps); printed moments use Shippori Mincho B1 ExtraBold Latin caps, tracking 0.4-0.6 em.
typography_rules.placement: Type never covers a face; it rides the world's verticals (poles, mirror poles, TV edge, moon path) or sits inside props.

render_rules.keyframe: Anima 1280x704. Every prompt starts with 'masterpiece, best quality, score_7, safe, anime screenshot, ' and uses the tokens verbatim. 4 candidates per shot; pick by token fidelity (bob with outward-flipped ends, mole under HER right eye, red neckerchief; his hair over his eyes). Negative: worst quality, low quality, text, watermark, signature, logo, silhouette, extra fingers, bad hands, deformed, nsfw, detailed background, scenery, gradient background.
render_rules.background: Flat green ('simple background, green background') for every keyed character: both leads wear white, so a white background would break the key. Two-person stills that are split into print plates use a white background and SAM masks instead of a key.
render_rules.video: Wan 2.2 TI2V 5B Turbo image-to-video at 640x352, 24 fps, frames 4n+1 (3.0 s = 73, 4.0 s = 97). Every video prompt keeps the camera static; all camera motion happens in three.js or the compositor.
render_rules.cutout: Chroma key the green (spill suppression, 1 px erode, matte smoothing); upscale x3 Lanczos to ~1920x1056; stylize with mvb/halftone.py PrintStyle using the shot's world inks (period 8, angle 45, XDoG line in #1A1416); sticker rim = 2 px warm-black line + 5 px cream #EDE3CF + 1.5 px vermilion hairline; optional drop shadow (+8,+8) in the world shadow ink at 60%. Beat-synced light is added in comp by modulating the halftone coverage on the lit side.
render_rules.still: Mesh-warp (puppet) animation of hair, cloth and small sways at 1-2 Hz, plus comp light changes. Stills are never face close-ups held longer than one bar.
render_rules.dots: Instanced dot-people with 8-12-frame cycles; the leads keep a colour ID (her: navy collar + red dot; him: white shirt + mint halo at night).
render_rules.reuse: A shot with mode 'still' and a 'source' field reuses keyframes or loops of earlier clips and generates nothing new.
render_rules.retime: Optical-flow (OpenCV DIS) retime only in B-bridge1-06 (0.68x, intended slow motion for the energy drop).

scene_list.S1: Tatami room (6 mats), 1985. CRT TV: 14-inch, wooden cabinet, rabbit-ear antenna, rotary channel dial with 30-degree click detents, screen = render target for any image/clip, generic sign-off card, generic test card (big centre circle, grey steps, colour bars), teletext ticker band; TV-POV rig (camera inside the CRT, barrel k=0.18, glass reflection layer, mirrored OSD). Oscillating fan (blade spin, 90-degree oscillation on a 2-bar period, stop and spin-down). Curtain (cloth, breathing). Window onto the railway with night / blue-hour plates. Folded futon, wall calendar (June 1985, page flutter), LED clock-radio (4-digit 7x13 dot clock + 64x8 mint ticker, colon blink on beats, fast-count mode 0:00 to 4:52), chabudai with the stamp-card plane and an empty ramune bottle, mosquito-coil smoke. Variants: night (TV on), sign-off (light stepping down on beats), blue-hour empty (TV off, afterglow dot).
scene_list.S2: Coastal road + seawall + railway. Lighting variants: noon, night, dusk (seawall), blue hour, dawn. Telephone poles at 16.3 m spacing (one per beat at 22 m/s) with catenary wires that sway; curve mirrors on orange poles (single, double-headed junction pole, a 40-mirror 'forest' variant, a giant title mirror), each mirror a render target with convex warp and ripple option; 2 vending machines plus a row of 6 on the seawall road (mint 16-dot ticker, 4-digit roulette, lit dummies, moth sprites); bus-stop sign and light box; concrete seawall with steps and railing, chalk-doodle decal slot and wave-wash; white lighthouse (rotating AM-halftone beam, lamp fade, red stamp box at the base, tower band for wrap-around type); sea (halftone waves, moon path, sun path, swell over the seawall); single-track rail alongside; wooden houses with eaves and 10 furin with tanzaku; asphalt with the mirage dot-melt shader and road-marking decal slots; a long straight for the dolly-zoom; invisible glyph planes for cast-shadow type.
scene_list.S3: Festival street / shotengai. Lanterns on wires (instanced, per-lantern emissive, glyph decal and swing), 10 hero lanterns spanning the street, yatai stalls (kingyo-sukui tank with 80 goldfish boids that can steer to a glyph mask and a paper poi with tear sim, mask stall, kakigori, yo-yo balloons), nobori banners, rolling shutters with an all-at-once roll-up, instanced dot crowd (1,200, both directions, parting behaviour, heads-up sprite), uchiwa fans with glyph flip. Variants: empty night (shutters down, unlit) and festival (lit, crowd).
scene_list.S4: Small station '潮見' + one-car train: platform, station-name board, lamp posts; train with an orange LED destination board (16x96: '回送', '夢 行', '日の出' + scrolling), lit windows each a render target with a per-window frame index (zoetrope), AM-halftone headlight; dream variant in two inks where the car is instanced into an endless chain for the zoetrope lock (one window pitch per frame); dawn variant passing behind the seawall.
scene_list.S5: Town map, oblique and top-down: coastline, railway, lighthouse and the 6 stamp locations; print-pass AOVs (navy, cobalt, orange, mint, silver) for print reveals; a navy night-plate sheet with paper-curl peel for the dawn; road ripple / re-route shader for the maze; stamp-route overlay (dashed to solid); map-label slots; window-light groups that can switch off on beats.
scene_list.S6: Underwater variant of S3: caustic line-screen projector, bubble emitter including glyph bubbles, lanterns floating up on slack wires, 60 goldfish boids, the surface seen from below with the moon as a wobbling disc.
scene_list.S7: School pool: 8 lanes, lane ropes with bobbing floats, starting blocks 1-8, amber LED scoreboard (8 rows: lane number, 16x16 name field, time) with a race clock '0:00.00', caustic water; noon and dawn variants.
